title: Tree Removal Permits Before Remodeling Shoreline WA — Significant Trees, Critical Areas, Arborist Reports and Tree Protection
description: A Shoreline homeowner's guide to trees before a remodel or addition: which trees are significant, when removal needs a permit, critical areas, replacement trees, arborist reports, tree protection fencing and root zones, street trees, and how it all fits with Shoreline permits.

search_intent: A Shoreline homeowner planning a remodel or addition wants to know which trees are regulated, when removal needs a permit, how many trees must be kept or replaced, when an arborist report is required, how trees must be protected during construction, and how tree review fits with Shoreline permits.
local_angles: SMC 20.50 Subchapter 5: tree cutting is clearing; additions are subject; tree materials submitted with the development application
Significant tree = 6 in DBH at 4.5 ft; 36-month removal allowance outside critical areas; >24 in DBH requires clearing and grading permit
Retention 35% (30% with critical areas); replacement 1-3 trees by DBH; conifers 6 ft, others 1.5 in caliper
SMC 20.50.370 protection: 6 ft chain-link barriers before land disturbance, no staging in critical root zone, project arborist on site, wood-chip mulch and summer water
Critical areas (SMC 20.80): trees of any size near streams, wetlands, steep slopes need City review
Street trees need a Right-of-Way Use Permit; Seattle City Light handles trees in power lines; Permit Services at City Hall, 17500 Midvale Ave N, (206) 801-2500; eTRAKiT
